name: apple-haptics
about: Timings, relative levels and pitches MEASURED from the demo videos on Apple's HIG 'Playing haptics' page (ffmpeg-decoded audio at 48 kHz, 60 fps video frames). IMPORTANT: the videos are ILLUSTRATIONS. Apple says they show bars 'and playing audio tones of different pitches' (iOS) and 'thin vertical lines that symbolize sound waves' (watchOS). The audio is a stand-in for the haptic, not the Taptic Engine waveform, so absolute Hz and dB are properties of the illustration; timings, ordering, crescendo/decrescendo and relative strength are the useful facts. No Apple video, audio or frame is committed.

tags.HIG: stated in the page text (names and meanings)
tags.MEASURED: measured from the page's demo audio/video (this repo, 2026-09-28)
tags.MEASURED-APPROX: measured, coarse (frame or window quantised): ±17 ms video timing, ±25 Hz pitch (iOS 20 ms tones), ±30 Hz (watch 24 ms window)
tags.CONV: apple-skill convention, not stated or measured from Apple

method.audio: ffmpeg → mono f32 48 kHz; 1–4 ms RMS envelope; events found by threshold and rise detection; pitch = FFT peak of each event (iOS) or STFT peak (watch, 24 ms Hann, 3 ms hop)
method.video: ffmpeg raw frames; frame 0 shows every event as a bar: bar HEIGHT = relative strength (5 steps 0.6–1.0), bar WIDTH = a duration/sharpness cue; a playhead flashes each bar when its sound plays
method.checks: flash times agree with audio onsets within one frame (≤ 17 ms); the light and dark video variants carry identical audio (same MD5); bar x-spacing is layout only (the playhead is non-linear), so event times come from the audio
method.limits: the illustration audio is not the actuator waveform; do not derive motor frequencies from it

ios.note: UIKit feedback generators: notification, impact, selection. relStrength = bar height / tallest bar (heavy impact = 1.0). peakAmp = linear peak of the illustration audio (full scale 1.0). t = ms from the first event.

success.meaning: a task or action has completed
success.shape: two taps, second stronger and slightly higher (crescendo, rising)

warning.meaning: a task or action produced a warning
warning.shape: two taps, second weaker and slightly lower (decrescendo, falling); slower than success

error.shape: two quick equal taps, then a strong hit, then a weaker longer low one; intervals widen 50 → 85 → 101 ms (ritardando)

light.meaning: collision between small or lightweight UI objects

medium.meaning: collision between medium-sized or medium-weight UI objects

heavy.meaning: collision between large or heavyweight UI objects

rigid.meaning: collision between hard or inflexible UI objects
rigid.shape: a broadband click (3 ms), the loudest and shortest of all iOS patterns, narrowest bar

soft.meaning: collision between soft or flexible UI objects
soft.shape: slowest attack (≈ 4× the others), higher pitch, widest bar

selection.meaning: a UI element's values are changing
selection.shape: the shortest tonal event, second-lightest after light impact

observations.massOrdering: light < medium < heavy: peak amplitude 0.185 → 0.387 → 0.692 and pitch 188 → 166 → 162 Hz (heavier = louder and lower)
observations.widthVsAttack: bar width tracks how soft the event feels: rigid 38 px (time-to-peak 1.4 ms) < selection 46 < light/medium/heavy 60 < soft 92 px (14.5 ms)
observations.multiEvent: success rises and grows, warning falls and shrinks, error is four events with a widening rhythm; direction and rhythm, not just count, carry the meaning
observations.flashVsAudio: flash and audio agree within 17 ms in every pattern

watchOS.note: t = ms from the first audible sample; carrier = pitch of the illustration tone; attacks = new onsets; to10pctMs = time until the envelope falls under 10 % of its peak.

notification.meaning: something significant or out of the ordinary needs attention; played when a local or remote notification arrives
notification.shape: one strong onset with a long decaying tail (the longest pattern)

up.meaning: an important value rose above a significant threshold
up.shape: two onsets; pitch steps UP 1.52 → 1.81 kHz

down.meaning: an important value fell below a significant threshold
down.shape: mirror of Up: pitch steps DOWN 1.81 → 1.52 kHz

success.shape: three onsets ~87 ms apart, pitch climbing 1.52 → 1.81 → 2.42 kHz

failure.shape: two light high taps (2.42 kHz), then one strong, sustained low hit (1.21 kHz, plateau ≈ 100 ms): pitch falls by an octave

retry.meaning: an action failed but can be retried
retry.shape: three onsets ~90 ms apart at ONE pitch (1.52 kHz): a rhythm with no rise or fall

start.meaning: an activity started (a timer, anything the person can start and stop); Stop usually follows

stop.meaning: an activity the person started has stopped
stop.shape: two identical Start-shaped onsets 294 ms apart, i.e. a doubled Start

click.meaning: a dial click: progress at predefined increments; overuse dilutes it and overlapping clicks confuse
click.shape: a single 9 ms broadband click, the shortest pattern; the illustration pitch is ≈ 4.9 kHz

observations.pitchVocabulary: the illustration uses ~1.2, 1.52, 1.81 and 2.42 kHz; rising pitch = positive/up/success, falling pitch = negative/down/failure, one flat pitch = neutral or repeat (retry, start, stop, notification)
observations.count: one onset = state or notice (notification, start, click); two = change of level (up, down) or end (stop); three = outcome or retry (success, failure, retry)
observations.carrierIntervals: 1.52 → 1.81 is a minor third, 1.81 → 2.42 a perfect fourth, 2.42 → 1.21 exactly one octave down (frequency ratios 1.19, 1.34, 0.5)
observations.duration: click 9 ms < start 231 < up 239 < down 261 < retry 388 < success 453 < failure 463 < stop 598 < notification 777 ms (audible)

patterns.alignment: the dragged item aligns with something, or reaches the start/end or min/max of a scrubber
patterns.levelChange: movement between discrete levels of pressure (e.g. fast-forward pressure levels)
patterns.generic: general feedback when the others don't apply

macOS.hardware: Magic Trackpad / Force Touch trackpad; API NSHapticFeedbackPerformer

eventTypes: continuous: sustained vibration (the lasers message effect)

rules: use system patterns only for their documented meanings
one clear cause-and-effect between an event and its haptic; never reuse a negative pattern for a positive outcome
complement visual and audio feedback; match intensity and sharpness to the animation it accompanies
don't overuse; the best haptic is one people miss when it is off
prefer short haptics for discrete events; long-running ones mostly suit gameplay flow (and are unpleasant on Apple Pencil Pro)
make sure vibration doesn't disturb camera, gyroscope or microphone experiences

webConv.src: CONV (not Apple; navigator.vibrate is supported on Android Chrome and similar, not on iOS Safari)
webConv.note: Vibration patterns are [on, off, on, …] milliseconds, DERIVED directly from the measured onsets and tone durations above (illustration audio durations, so they are not actuator times). Phone motors need a longer pulse than these to be felt: clamp every 'on' to at least minOnMs and re-tune on a real device.
webConv.retryNote: retry is the watchOS pattern: three onsets ~90 ms apart; 'on' times are not measured separately, 22 ms is a CONV guess
